name: Salvinorin A

binding.tissue_or_cell: HEK293 transiently expressing human cloned KOR (cloned receptor)
binding.radioligand_or_probe: [3H]-bremazocine (competition); 48 secondary targets in PDSP screen showed no significant displacement

binding.tissue_or_cell: HEK293 transiently expressing FLAG-His6-tagged human KOR

biased_agonism.bias_reference_compound: Salvinorin A is used as the unbiased reference (bias factor = 1) in White/Roth 2015
biased_agonism.interpretation: Salvinorin A recruits both G-protein and β-arrestin pathways with roughly balanced potency; β-arrestin recruitment is implicated in the dysphoric/aversive component shared by all unbiased KOR agonists.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: KOR Gαi/o coupling → adenylyl cyclase inhibition (decreased cAMP) and Gβγ-mediated GIRK channel activation and N/P/Q-type calcium channel inhibition. Salvinorin A also robustly activates β-arrestin-2 recruitment with subsequent JNK activation and KOR desensitisation/internalisation — these pathways underlie the rapid tachyphylaxis and dysphoric/aversive component characteristic of unbiased KOR agonism.

neuroimaging.finding: Baboon brain uptake peaked at ~40 s after IV bolus reaching 3.3% of injected dose; brain clearance half-life ~8 min — matches the <10-min behavioural duration after smoking in humans.

neuroimaging.modality: fMRI BOLD (12 healthy men, 15 µg/kg inhaled vapor)
neuroimaging.finding: Decreased within-network static functional connectivity, increased between-network connectivity, reduced dynamic FC, increased FC entropy. Most prominent effect: attenuation of default mode network (DMN) during first half of 20-min scan (F(1,11) = 9.40, p = 0.011; every subject showed DMN reduction, d = 1.50). Effect tracks the 1–10 min peak subjective intensity.
Reduced resting EEG spectral power across most bands (Ranganathan/Krystal, Yale).

routes.subject_demographics: Healthy adults, mean age 25, 4× received 21 µg/kg and 2× received 18 µg/kg vaporised via glass pipe
routes._note: Johnson/Reissig — Cmax mean 18.8 ng/mL at 2 min; subjective intensity correlated with plasma level r ≈ 0.93 across subjects; prolactin rose from 5 min peaking at 15 min, cortisol inconsistent. Effects essentially gone by 20 min, plasma near baseline by 90 min.

Up to 4 mg sublingual produced no psychoactive effects — very low bioavailability via the DMSO/PEG-400 sublingual vehicle (review citing Ranganathan).  Buccal absorption of leaf-extract juice held >10 min in mouth is the traditional Mazatec route.
Effectively zero oral bioavailability — rapid GI hydrolysis of C2 acetate to inactive salvinorin B; P-gp efflux at BBB.

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: CYP2D6 contributes ~15% of in-vitro metabolism — theoretically PMs could see slightly higher exposure but the dominant clearance pathway is plasma esterase hydrolysis (independent of CYP), so PM/UM status is unlikely to change clinical PK meaningfully.

tolerance_and_dependence.receptor_downregulation_half_time: Acute desensitisation of KOR within minutes of salvinorin A exposure in HEK293 (β-arrestin-dependent); rapid tachyphylaxis to subjective effects when redosing within tens of minutes is reported anecdotally but not formally quantified in humans.
tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: No physical withdrawal syndrome described; KOR agonists produce dysphoria/anhedonia acutely rather than dependence on cessation.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: A 2008 report suggested partial agonism at D2 (Ki 5-10 nM, 40-60% intrinsic activity); subsequent work has not consistently replicated this and the contribution to in-vivo effects is unclear.
No appreciable binding (PDSP screen, Roth 2002) — mechanistically distinguishes Sal A from classical psychedelics.

data_gaps_remaining: Human Vd, CL, AUC, protein binding
6-hydroxynorsalvinorin metabolite — could not confirm primary literature; salvinorin B is the dominant documented metabolite

name: Salvinorin B

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Negligible KOR engagement — its biological role is as the inactive principal metabolite of salvinorin A and as a synthetic precursor to the C-2 ether analogues (MOM-Sal B, EOM-Sal B, mesyl Sal B).

data_gaps_remaining: Precise Ki value at human KOR — most papers simply report >1 µM

name: Salvinorin E
data_gaps_remaining: Definitive Ki value — literature reports a range from 65 nM to >10 µM depending on assay/source

name: Salvinorin F
data_gaps_remaining: Quantitative Ki not extracted from primary paper

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: MOR antagonist activity reported. Salvinicin B is notable because it inverts the opioid receptor selectivity of the salvinorin scaffold from KOR-agonist to MOR-antagonist, showing how plastic the scaffold is.

biased_agonism.interpretation: Originally reported as a strongly G-protein-biased MOR agonist (Groer et al. 2007 — induces MAPK signalling but does not recruit β-arrestin-2 or internalise MOR even with GRK2 overexpression). Later studies (Manglik/Shoichet group) reported similar β-arrestin recruitment to DAMGO depending on assay/cell-system — bias is contested. The original observation made herkinorin a landmark tool compound for MOR-biased agonism research.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: MOR Gαi/o coupling; G-protein-mediated MAPK activation; minimal β-arrestin-2 recruitment / internalisation in HEK293 + GRK2 assay (Groer 2007); contested by later studies.

tolerance_and_dependence.receptor_downregulation_half_time: Hypothesised to be slower than morphine — minimal internalisation should mean reduced tolerance development. Not formally measured in humans.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Binds both KOR and MOR; in piglet cerebral vessels its vasodilation is abolished by a KOR antagonist and unaffected by a MOR antagonist, so it is not MOR-selective in function.

binding.tissue_or_cell: HEK293 transiently expressing FLAG-His6-tagged human KOR

biased_agonism.interpretation: Bias factor 96 toward G-protein over β-arrestin-2 (relative to Sal A as the unbiased reference). One of the most strongly G-protein-biased KOR agonists ever reported — the prototype for the 'Gi-biased KOR agonist = non-dysphoric analgesic' hypothesis. In vivo: analgesic without the locomotor incoordination seen with unbiased KOR agonists; retains aversion (so Gi bias does not fully eliminate dysphoria).

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Strong Gαi/o-mediated cAMP inhibition and GIRK activation with markedly reduced β-arrestin-2 recruitment and receptor internalisation. Irreversible (covalent) tethering to KOR via the C-22 reactive group → very long-duration KOR activation.

tolerance_and_dependence.receptor_downregulation_half_time: Reduced KOR internalisation compared to unbiased agonists — predicted to develop tolerance more slowly, though formal time-course not in literature.

name: 22-Thiocyanatosalvinorin A

binding.tissue_or_cell: HEK293 transiently expressing FLAG-His6-tagged human KOR

biased_agonism.interpretation: Bias factor 96. Sustained G-protein analgesia with markedly reduced β-arrestin-2 recruitment and reduced motor incoordination.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Same as Mesyl Sal B entry — covalent irreversible KOR agonism; very long apparent duration.

data_gaps_remaining: Human exposure data — research compound only

biased_agonism.interpretation: G-protein-biased in cellular assays. Substitution of C-2 ethoxymethyl ether for the C-2 acetyl group of Sal A reduces JNK stimulation, prevents desensitisation, and gives a monotonic antinociceptive dose-response. Associated with anti-cocaine efficacy with fewer KOR side effects (less anxiogenic/anhedonic).

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: KOR Gαi/o (cAMP↓, GIRK↑) with reduced β-arrestin-2 recruitment and reduced JNK activation. In MS preclinical models (EAE) shows KOR-dependent disease modification — possibly via myelin-OL-progenitor effects.

tolerance_and_dependence.receptor_downregulation_half_time: Reduced acute desensitisation vs Sal A (Bruchas group — C-2 ether prevents the rapid JNK-mediated KOR desensitisation seen with Sal A).

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Full-agonist KOR activation, ~5–7× more potent than U50488 / Sal A in GTPγS. Internalises and downregulates KOR similarly to Sal A and U50488 — so unlike EOM Sal B or RB-64, MOM Sal B is not biased; it's a balanced KOR full agonist with extended duration.

metabolism.enzyme: Resistant to plasma esterase hydrolysis (vs Sal A acetate)

tolerance_and_dependence.receptor_downregulation_half_time: Similar internalisation/downregulation to Sal A and U50488 in vitro.

name: 16-Bromo-salvinorin A

binding.tissue_or_cell: HEK293 expressing human KOR (also DAT-KOR coexpressed)

biased_agonism.interpretation: Reported as G-protein-biased KOR agonist, contrasting with the more balanced 16-ethynyl Sal A. Anti-cocaine efficacy without significant effects on locomotion, food reward, learning/memory, anxiety, or depression — supports the hypothesis that KOR G-bias drives the desirable effects.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: G-protein-biased KOR agonism with reduced KOR-mediated DAT internalisation effects on dopamine signalling compared to Sal A.

data_gaps_remaining: Human exposure data — research compound only

name: IBOGAINE

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: MISCLASSIFIED FOR THIS GROUP. Ibogaine is an iboga-alkaloid tabernanthe constituent (indole alkaloid, complex polypharmacology at NMDA / κ-opioid / 5-HT2A / 5-HT-transporter / sigma-2 / nAChR α3β4) — it is not a salvinorin neoclerodane diterpene and does not belong in the 'dysdelics and KOR ligands (salvinorin family)' group as a salvinorin sibling. Ibogaine does have weak KOR agonism, but its primary mechanism of action is debated and most studied as a polypharmacological agent. Recommend reassigning to an iboga / atypical-psychedelic group for proper enrichment.

data_gaps_remaining: Ibogaine should be enriched by an iboga-alkaloid-focused agent — out of scope for this salvinorin-focused pass.

shared_mechanism: Neoclerodane diterpenes from Salvia divinorum and their semi-synthetic analogues are the only known non-nitrogenous agonists of the κ-opioid receptor (KOR). They bind KOR in a binding pocket distinct from the classical morphinan/peptide site: salvinorin A occupies the extracellular portion of the KOR cavity, with the C-4 methyl ester hydrogen-bonding to Glu297(ECL2), the C-1 carbonyl to Tyr312(7.35), and the C-2 acetoxy to Tyr313(7.36), with the furan ring pointing down into the morphinan pocket (PDB 6B73 / Roth 2021). Crucially they lack the protonatable amine that all classical opioids use to engage Asp138(3.32). Downstream they couple via Gαi/o to cAMP inhibition and GIRK activation, with substantial β-arrestin-2 recruitment that drives KOR desensitisation, JNK activation, and the dysphoric/aversive component of the subjective experience. The phenomenology produced — rapid dissociation, intense 'shifting reality' visuals, dysphoria — does not involve 5-HT2A (no classical-psychedelic mechanism) or NMDA (no classical-dissociative mechanism), making the class mechanistically third-kind. The term 'dysdelic' coined to capture this neither-psychedelic-nor-dissociative phenomenology.
shared_pk_summary: All members of this class are highly lipophilic, non-ionisable, and bind plasma albumin tightly. Smoked/inhaled, salvinorin A reaches Cmax in 2 min (mean ~19 ng/mL after 21 µg/kg) and plasma levels return to baseline within 90 min; brain uptake peaks within 40 s (baboon PET) and clears with t½ ~8 min — explaining the <10 min subjective duration. Oral bioavailability is essentially zero due to rapid GI esterase hydrolysis of the C-2 acetate to inactive salvinorin B. The C-2 acetate is the metabolically labile group — replacing it with C-2 ether (MOM, EOM), sulfonate (mesyl), or other ester (benzoate — herkinorin) dramatically extends duration (≥100-fold in some cases) by preventing esterase hydrolysis. In vitro: salvinorin A is metabolised by plasma carboxylesterase (dominant), with secondary contributions from CYP2D6, CYP1A1, CYP2C18, CYP2E1, and UGT2B7. P-gp is an efflux substrate at the BBB. Sublingual/buccal absorption needs DMSO/PEG vehicle; aqueous vehicles fail (logP ~2.5 but poor water solubility).
shared_safety: Cardiopulmonary safety appears favourable in clinical doses studied (modest, transient increases in HR/BP at peak effect). The principal acute harm-reduction concerns are: (1) profound dissociation/loss of body awareness within seconds of smoking — risk of physical injury / wandering / unintended self-harm — making a tripsitter essential; (2) acute dysphoria and lasting emotional residue from intense β-arrestin-driven KOR signalling; (3) lack of cross-tolerance with classical psychedelics — even experienced psychedelic users are caught off-guard by Sal A's intensity and short rebuild time; (4) seizure-like motor phenomena documented at high doses. Hormonal: increases prolactin (peaks ~15 min after inhalation) and inconsistently cortisol. The semi-synthetic C-2-modified analogues (MOM Sal B, RB-64, 16-Br Sal A) have markedly extended duration — same dose intensity but lasting hours rather than minutes, magnifying all harms.
sar_summary: The Sal A pharmacophore requires: (1) the C-4 methyl ester (loss → loss of activity); (2) the furan ring at C-12 (loss → near-complete loss of activity; halogenation at C-16 of furan tolerated and even extends duration without losing potency — see 16-Br Sal A); (3) the C-2 ester/ether on the alpha-face (de-acetylation → Sal B, essentially inactive); the C-1 carbonyl is NOT strictly required (the 1-deoxy analogue is well-tolerated); the C-2 hydroxyl orientation matters — beta-epimer dramatically less active. The C-2 acetoxy is the key modifiable position for therapeutic engineering: methyl ester (Sal A) → 100× extended duration as methoxymethyl ether (MOM Sal B / SymBMS) → biased agonist as ethoxymethyl ether (EOM Sal B) → biased irreversible agonist as 22-thiocyanate/sulfonate (RB-64). Replacement of acetate with benzoate (herkinorin) inverts receptor selectivity from KOR to MOR. C-1, C-12, C-16, and C-22 modifications all generate distinct G-protein-bias profiles, making the salvinorin scaffold one of the richest classes for biased-agonism SAR alongside the morphinan/MOR field. Salvinicin A/B (cyclic 12,17-rearrangements) demonstrate further plasticity — Sal A becomes a KOR partial agonist, Sal B a MOR antagonist.
